title: How do we change these fractions into decimals?
description: Four fractions with bottom numbers ten, a hundred and a thousand are written as decimals, digit by digit. A last step turns one decimal back into a fraction.
teaching_notes: One idea: the bottom number says which places the digits sit in, and empty places get zeros. Watch for children who drop the zeros after the point.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q1
video_script.why: The child has written fractions as decimals one at a time and now does four in a row.
video_script.substitution: The bottom number says which places the digits sit in, and empty places get zeros.
video_script.anchor: four fractions with bottom numbers ten, a hundred and a thousand
video_script.payoff_line: The bottom number tells us where each digit sits

final_answer.spoken: zero point zero five, zero point zero one six, one point two and zero point two five four

video_script.fraction_reading: five over a hundred, sixteen over a thousand and similar are said in words
video_script.design: The four fractions stay in the anchor band; each is placed in the place value chart in the working band, and a last step turns 0.016 back into a fraction.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four fractions (a) 5/100 (b) 16/1000 (c) 12/10 (d) 254/1000; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about changing fractions into decimals.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Four fractions are given, with bottom numbers ten, a hundred and a thousand.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each fraction in decimal form, one by one.

beats.on_screen: the fractions stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a place value chart: units, a point, tenths, hundredths and thousandths

marks.chart: the chart of places is drawn
marks.bottom: the bottom numbers 10, 100 and 1000 are matched to the places

narration: <bookmark mark='chart'/>Here is the place value chart, with tenths, hundredths and thousandths after the point.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>A bottom number of ten, a hundred or a thousand tells us how many places we need.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five over a hundred and sixteen over a thousand.
Also twelve over ten and two hundred fifty-four over a thousand.

beats.on_screen: To find: each fraction as a decimal
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each fraction as a decimal.

marks.az: a zero fills the tenths place and 0.05 is written
marks.b: 1 and 6 drop into hundredths and thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, five over a hundred is five hundredths, so the five sits in the hundredths place.
<bookmark mark='az'/>The tenths place is empty, so we write zero point zero five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Sixteen over a thousand is one hundredth and six thousandths.
<bookmark mark='bw'/>We write it as zero point zero one six.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 12/10 = 1 unit + 2 tenths = 1.2; 254/1000 = 2 tenths + 5 hundredths + 4 thousandths = 0.254

marks.c: 12/10 is split into 1 unit and 2 tenths, and 1.2 is written
marks.d: 2, 5 and 4 drop into tenths, hundredths and thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step two, twelve over ten is one unit and two tenths, so it is one point two.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Two hundred fifty-four over a thousand is two tenths, five hundredths and four thousandths.
<bookmark mark='dw'/>We write it as zero point two five four.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Step three, put the answers back by turning one decimal into a fraction again.
Zero point zero one six is ten thousandths plus six thousandths.
<bookmark mark='same'/>That is sixteen thousandths, the same as the fraction we began with.

marks.first: the first two answers are marked
marks.last: the last two answers are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The bottom number tells us where each digit sits.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two are zero point zero five and zero point zero one six.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last two are one point two and zero point two five four.
